sources.note: Direct official description and Outstanding Universal Value: capital 1802, dynasty until 1945; citadel, geomancy, forts and hydraulic network.

sources.title: Imperial Archives of the Nguyen Dynasty, UNESCO Memory of the World nomination
sources.note: Direct PDF: printed3 dynasty and administrative records; printed9 Form and style, do paper, brush, handwriting recruitment, red imperial annotations.

sources.title: Vietnam National Museum of History, Quang Nam from 1801 to 1832
sources.note: Direct museum account, final paragraphs: Minh Mang provincial reorganization in 1831 and 1832, thirty provinces.

sources.title: Vietnam National Museum of History, The Nguyen dynasty and Christianity
sources.note: Direct museum article: Minh Mang prohibition in 1832 and Tu Duc coercion culminating in 1861 dispersal policy. Do not generalize source political accusations to all Christians.

sources.title: Vietnam National Museum of History, Reconstructing the final phase of Hoang Dinh Kinh resistance through Tonkin commissioner records
sources.note: Indexed original opening: 1858 Franco-Spanish invasion at Da Nang, 1862 cession of Gia Dinh, Dinh Tuong, Bien Hoa and Con Lon. Use year only; museum month conflicts with conventional landing date.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States 1883, document 485: treaty signed at Hue on 25 August 1883
sources.note: Direct diplomatic transcription of Harmand treaty in enclosure: articles I, XI, XIV, XVIII and XIX. This is the 1883 agreement, not the revised 1884 Patenotre treaty.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States 1885, document 264: France-China treaty of 9 June 1885
sources.note: Direct treaty, article2 commitment by China to respect France-Annam treaties; article1 withdrawal/non-entry of Chinese troops.

sources.title: Woodblocks of Nguyen Dynasty, UNESCO Memory of the World nomination
sources.note: Original PDF indexed text, summary p1 and p3 rare works. Direct open returned no extractable text. Hán/Nôm reverse-carving for printing official histories, laws, literature and classics. Counts omitted because later conservation accounts differ.

sources.title: Ueda Shinya, Family Structure in Early Modern Vietnam: Villages around Hue, Southeast Asian Studies 12(2), 2023
sources.note: Direct full paper. SectionI-1 local garden cadasters, conclusion compound households and residence variation; III-3 Case1 exactly dated women land transactions. Widow identification only inferred and omitted. Evidence combines late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; dates explicitly scoped.

sources.title: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism, Hue garden houses bloom with beauty
sources.note: Direct official tourism-hosted account: An Hien late nineteenth-century construction and surviving timber house, courtyard and garden. Modern plants are not treated as an inventory from the 1800s; questionable ownership genealogy omitted.

sources.title: Vietnam National Museum of History, Nguyen education and examinations, part 2
sources.note: Direct opening royal education schedule: classics on odd days, history on even days; afternoons of lunar6,16,26 bring books to Quang Minh hall for emperor review. Elite practice, no claim universal schooling.

sources.title: C. Michele Thompson, French Colonial Medicine in Indo-China, p. 331
sources.note: Indexed original p331 and note9. Despiau sent Macau July1820, returned February1821 with vaccine, royal children vaccinated, ten physicians taught. Note9: no evidence this early programme spread outside royal circles. Direct PDF failed; query exact URL plus 1821 recovers passage.

sources.title: Vietnam archives, A hospital for Nguyen eunuchs and female officials
sources.note: Indexed full original, 10 July2022: Binh An duong founded October1823 under imperial medical service for ill court servants, relatives could help care. Later Duy Tan building measurements and modern herb garden deliberately omitted.

sources.title: Vietnam archives, The river through the heart of Hue
sources.note: Direct archive account: Ngu Ha east1805/west1825, royal granaries and transport of rice/salt/money/metals; stone banks and dredging documents. No claim of universal domestic sanitation.

sources.title: Vietnam archives, First Full Moon Festival and ceremonial offerings at the Nguyen court
sources.note: Direct article: 1835 Minh Mang decree, Dai Nam thuc luc vol4 p748; fruit/tea/foods for selected festivals and all-night lanterns at First Full Moon and Mid-Autumn. Court-specific evidence.

sources.title: Collection of Nguyen reward coins at the Vietnam National Museum of History
sources.note: Direct five-page scholarly museum article; PDFp2 section2.2 and indexed original confirm gold LSb.34836 diameter3.2cm, obverse明命通寶, reverse富壽多男, reading Phú thọ đa nam, Vietnamese translation Giàu có, sống lâu, nhiều con trai. English translation supplied from explicit Vietnamese gloss. Chinese PDF extraction garbled but exact script independently recovered in indexed original with query URL plus 富 Phú. Dates safely described as Minh Mang era,1820s/1830s; no invented precise minting year.
